what_happened: Task description hypothesized a path-resolution defect in validate-wiring.sh. Reproduction in the plan dispatch showed all 41 failures come from the .opencode arm of a --all run where the files genuinely do not exist (0 of 41 resolve); .claude alone is green. Actual defects: (1) the FAIL message omits the system tree and resolved path, making the verdict unauditable; (2) the committed .opencode/context/index.json carries 41 dangling entries for memory/nix/nvim extensions that tree has no manifest for. Plan targets both rather than the hypothesized resolution bug.

Root cause fully established within the plan dispatch using only script invocations and greps: --claude vs --opencode arm split, per-tree file existence spot-checks, index entry counts, and a resolve-every-entry loop. No research round was needed, and the existing test-validate-wiring.sh fixture harness already supplies the model for the both-directions fixture the acceptance criterion requires.
